title: Best movie to watch while high?

commenti.body: [removed]

My first thought was Stalker so I definitely agree with you there. I think more atmospheric cinema that communicates more through aesthetics and feelings rather than plot and dialogue are perfect for being high. For that I would recommend Taste of Cherry, And Life Goes On, Pickpocket, and Certain Women.

When I was younger, the police stopped and searched me and found my bag of weed. When I was detained, they asked what my plans were for the evening. I told them that I was going to get stoned and watch the DVD I had in my bag -- Paprika directed by Satoshi Kon, the anime film about a machine that allows people to travel into dreams. 

The police officer said, 'Well, at least you'll be able to enjoy the movie properly now'. 

What an idiot. I could hardly think of a movie you could enjoy more while high than Paprika.

Definitely The Big Lebowski. It’s pretty much THE stoner movie in my opinion. The deliberately meandering plot, the eccentric characters, the self-referential humor and weird dialogue tangents is meant to evoke the state of being high. Can’t recommend it enough.

Persona and The Lighthouse are two of my favorites for their surrealism, unreliable narrators and general ambiguity. Chungking Express is another great watch. Incredibly emotionally affecting and great aesthetics, particularly the color palette. Ran and Blade Runner 2049 for similar reasons (though very different movies).

Or basically any scifi or scifi adjacent movie that has a superficially simplistic premise that reveals layers of depth that take multiple watches to unpack, all but guaranteeing them as cult classics that will divide casual viewers, high falutting critics and basement dwelling incel uber geeks equally in their assessment.

Most of that was just to meet r/truefilm's stupid fucking minimum word count

A few films I have enjoyed in such a state: Head (1968), The Double Life of Veronique (1991), Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975), Valerie and Her Week of Wonders (1970).

I also want to make special mention of Robert Altman’s filmography. The overlapping dialogue, the long takes, the washed out color palette- it’s a perfect fit. My favorites of his are McCabe and Mrs. Miller, California Split, The Long Goodbye, 3 Women, A Wedding, Thieves Like Us… too many to name actually.

Stalker is very much about dialogue though.

Apocalypse Now. 

The changes in scenery from each stop along the trip feel so surreal when not high, and are even better when high. Some of the scenes are just jarring enough that you question whether it’s you or the film.

Definitely one of my favorite high movie experiences.
Did he though? I rewatched that scene and he still sounded like a paranoid nut. But at least he wasn't harassing the families of murdered children. God what a piece of shit.

I just want to second 2001. It's the perfect pace movie for being high and the visuals are so engaging and the music is great. It's just a joy all around. I can assure you you'll be glued to the screen for the whole runtime.  I loved watching this movie high.

I'm super about atmosphere when it comes to this. Brazil, Heat, Total Recall, The Departed, American Beauty, and Days of Heaven are all specifically enjoyable experiences that I remember.

Indiana Jones becomes kind of unintentionally hilarious because if you picture Indy as a real person you start to realize how much of a reckless psycho he is. This can apply to anything with a conventional lead whose lunatic level behavior is framed in a straightforward heroic fashion.

"Monkey Shines" is one of those good bad movies (to me) that is even better high.

Based on a very old memory, The Monkees movie "Head" was really great when high.

I'd also recommend "Hush, Hush Sweet Charlotte" (an old B&W Bette Davis horror movie)

My recommendation would be Kin-dza-dza! Totally not based on my own experience. I remember a time when it was the highest rated film on IMDb.

Seeing Spirited Away for the first time was quite an experience too. The pig scene freaked me out. Probably any Miyazaki would work.

Weekend at Bernie's. For some reason it really heightened the subtle offbeat moods, slightly unnatural dialogue, the vivid colors. Loved it. Never tried watching Wake in Fright stoned, though, the prospect is a bit scary.

As already mentioned here I think the Big Lebowski is a perfect stoner movie. Adding to that I would recommend Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, and Inherent Vice which has similar tones to Lebowski but in a different way.

For me, the first thing that comes to mind is the 2003 film, **Interstella 5555: The 5tory of the 5ecret 5tar 5ystem**.
The daft punk soundtrack, and visual flow of the movie is awesome.

Right, the mods could fairly delete this post. If you had just listed the movies, it’s true that you would have come in under the (very small) minimum req. My point is that that reflects less on your comment then on the post itself, which is not the type of thing they’re trying to foster here.

I don’t mean to just simp for the mod rules though, because the recommendations here, including yours, are much more interesting than you’d get in most other movie subs.
"I shouldn't have smoked that shit, now I'm in The Zone"

I can see where they're coming from, there are multiple other subs devoted just to recs rather than (attempts at) analysis. The minimum word count still strikes me as incredibly stupid, nonetheless. To paraphrase Twain, "I didn't have time to write you a short letter, so I wrote you a long one"

That's true the dialogue is important, but more in ways that are thought provoking and philosophical, rather than communicating plot details that are integral to following the story. For example, I had a hard time enjoying Oppenheimer because I wasn't following the dialogue, yet I had no problem enjoying Stalker when I missed plenty of the dialogue while admiring the visual beauty. 

That said, there is still plenty of plot and exposition communicated through dialogue in Stalker, so maybe I'm contradicting myself here, I just find it to be different. It speaks to my soul more than my brain.
Yeah, on one hand, the count is so low that a tiny amount of words clears the bar (this comment is 194 char's). On the other hand, it's really annoying and doesn't do much to improve discussion.

My "go to"s are either silly comedies (Hot Rod, Wet Hot American Summer, Barb & Star Go to Vista Del Mar), films with interesting visuals (seconding Waking Life and Paprika, throwing in Samsara) or weird movies (Ghost World, Funny Pages, Wrong, Tokyo).

I mean, I watch all sorts of stuff while baked, but those kinds of movies are usually a guaranteed good time for me.

I find horror films can be hit or miss for me when I’m high. Maybe it’s just me but even well made horror like hereditary I’ve watched baked and idk, it’s like my brain decided it was a comedy towards the end instead. 


3rd for 2001 tho. Or any Kubrick film for that matter

Donnie Darko, Mulholland Drive (Anything by David Lynch really) The Warriors, Requiem for a Dream, Memento, Fight Club, Taxi Driver, A Clockwork Orange, Drive, Midsommar. These are a few I think of from the top of my head.

I don't think your stoned brain misread the ending of hereditary. It did get kind of silly towards the end and it threw so much stuff at that same time that it gave me a real "wtf am I watching now?" feeling and I wasn't high. I found the first half of that movie so much scarier than the second half.
